      "body": "There is no host uniqueness validation or database constraint, so the Add Host action can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including case variants. record_for_host selects only the first matching row, so editing another displayed mapping has no effect on where imported topics are posted, and deleting one row may leave the host authorized by another. findings.title: Migration fails when no embed category is configured
findings.body: The category query is indexed with `[0]['id']` before checking whether it returned any rows. Sites using the default empty embed_category, sites without that setting stored, and sites whose configured category was deleted will return no rows and raise instead of reaching the uncategorized fallback. This prevents otherwise valid installations from completing the upgrade. Handle an empty result before accessing the first row.

findings.title: Normalize existing hosts before inserting them
findings.body: The migration copies old host entries verbatim through SQL, bypassing the new model's normalization callback. The previous host check explicitly supported entries such as `https://eviltrout.com`, but the new lookup compares the stored value directly with URI.host (`eviltrout.com`). Such entries are migrated successfully but no longer authorize embedding or topic retrieval. Normalize the migrated entries before deleting the old settings so existing supported configurations continue to work.

findings.title: Hosts saved with a port can never match
findings.body: The host validator accepts values such as `example.com:8080`, and normalization preserves the port, but record_for_host extracts only URI.host and queries for `example.com`. Consequently, an allowed host saved with a port never authorizes any request, including requests from that exact host and port, and its category mapping is never used. Make storage and lookup use the same host/port representation.

findings.title: Host validation rejects valid longer top-level domains
findings.body: The top-level domain is limited to two through five letters, rejecting valid domains such as `example.museum`, `example.online`, and `example.technology`. Administrators cannot add these sites to the embedding allowlist even though they are valid hosts. Use hostname validation that supports current top-level domains rather than this length restriction.

findings.title: Prevent multiple category mappings for the same host
findings.body: There is no host uniqueness validation or database constraint, so the Add Host action can save the same hostname multiple times with different categories, including case variants. record_for_host selects only the first matching row, so editing another displayed mapping has no effect on where imported topics are posted, and deleting one row may leave the host authorized by another. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname so each displayed relationship has an unambiguous effect.
